 SNDK -5.35%

 Learn more Semiconductor stocks rebounded Tuesday, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) rising as major chipmakers bounced following steep losses. 
 Shares of memory chipmaker Micron Technology ( MU ) jumped 2%, reversing some of Monday's 7% decline. Peer SK Hynix ( SKHY ), along with memory and storage names Sandisk ( SNDK ), Seagate ( STX ), and Western Digital ( WDC ), also opened higher. 
 AI chipmakers Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ) rallied 3% and 5%, respectively. AMD shares erased some of their 7% losses from the prior session, ahead of the company's quarterly results due after the closing bell Tuesday. 
 Elsewhere, Broadcom ( AVGO ) edged up 3%, while Intel ( INTC ) jumped 1% after an 8% decline on Monday.

NVDA AMD AVGO As Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre pointed out, chip and memory stocks have lost about $3.7 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Nvidia lost the most in dollar terms, but Intel's nearly 50% drop is the steepest among the giants. 
 Semiconductor companies have been key beneficiaries of the AI build-out. Concerns over AI spending and neocloud debt weighed on the sector in recent weeks.
